newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Products - Gulf gasolines barrel higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Products - Gulf gasolines barrel higher.

text.p: U.S. Gulf gasoline differentials jumped higher by midday Tuesday as fresh buying interest in both the conventional and reformulated grades emerged there, market players said.

Outright gasoline prices also got a boost as the June NYMEX contract rebounded from its early weakness to hit 66.00 cents a gallon, up 0.79 cent. June heating oil was up 0.48 cent at 58.40 cents a gallon.

Prompt conventional M1 gasoline differentials firmed to about 2.90 cents under the June NYMEX, up about 0.50 cents from Monday, while late May barrels were said to have traded at 3.25 cents under the June earlier in the day.
Prompt reformulated gasoline was talked between about 0.10 and 0.35 cent over the June NYMEX, also 0.50 cent stronger on the day, helped by fresh refinery interest traders said.

The outage at Phillips' Sweeny, Texas refinery last week and the slight delays that will prevent it from returning to normal operations until the end of this week pushed the company into the spot market.
"They were out trying to buy A grades," said one Gulf Coast player.

Products were quiet again on Tuesday, with traders calling market prices difficult to gauge. In Group Three, unleaded gasoline by delivery today was heard trading at 7.80 cents over June NYMEX gasoline, while end-of-month barrels remained at 5.25/5.50 cents over the screen.
Group Three prompt premium differentials were a tad weaker at 3.00 cents over, traders said.
In the Chicago markets, which were also quiet, unleaded gasoline traded at 2.25 cents over the screen for prompt delivery. Any months were pegged even.
Despite the strength in the U.S. Gulf gasoline, traders said Harbor levels remained flat in early Tuesday trade, with prompt conventional M2 gasoline seen near 2.00 cents under the June NYMEX.

Distillate levels were also seen steady, with low sulphur diesel for prompt delivery talked on either side of 0.60 cents under the June NYMEX, and prompt heating oil seen near 0.15 cent under the June.
